title: Streaming typed contract recovery cross-model harness
creator: Ariana Chen
description: Build an automated harness that validates typed/JSON-style contract adherence for streaming responses across multiple model variants and runtime configurations, especially when tool/function calls and partial streaming fragments occur. The harness should exercise: partial-token truncation, backpressure-induced chunking, interleaved toolcall annotations, KV cache warm vs cold conditions, and quantized model variants. Goal is to detect silent contract degradations and verify recovery/fallback behavior (tolerant parser, sentinel insertion, and retry policies).
acceptance_criteria: Harness can replay 10k synthetic streaming sessions with injected faults and surface a per-session contract verdict (pass/warn/fail)

For sessions where streaming is interrupted mid-object, system must detect malformed JSON and validate that the configured recovery strategy (sentinel close + incremental reassembly) leads to a deterministic verdict within 2s
Tool/function call annotations inside streams must not break typed-decoder: test vector set covers nested tool calls and asserts fields are present/typed after reassembly
Cross-model run: at least 3 model families (base fp16, int8-quantized, and a proprietary tuned variant) show consistent pass/fail classification for the same prompts
Harness produces a CSV summary and per-session debug artifacts (raw token stream, decoder traces, KV-cache state) for any failing sessions
tasks: Design harness architecture and storage layout for artifacts (S3 paths, local ephemeral) - owner: Marcus
Implement stream reassembly simulator capable of emitting arbitrary chunk boundaries and backpressure timings - owner: Lea Morales
Create synthetic prompt suite including nested tool calls, arrays-of-objects, and edge-case separators - owner: Marcus
Integrate typed-decoder gate and tolerant fallback parser into harness pipeline - owner: Rahul Gupta
Add cross-model runner that swaps kernel/quantization profiles and toggles KV-cache warm/cold - owner: Deepa Rao
Build CI job that runs 500 sessions nightly and uploads failures to the incident dashboard - owner: SRE team
Document failure modes and recommended runtime mitigations for Console rollout - owner: PM (Aisha)
test_plan: Scenario A - Clean stream: full JSON object emitted in single chunk (sanity)
Scenario B - Fragmented object: object split across multiple chunks at random token boundaries
Scenario C - Truncated stream: stream ends mid-object then resumed by retry; validate reassembly and de-duplication
Scenario D - Interleaved toolcall metadata: toolcall start/end markers arrive in separate chunks and with injected latency
Scenario E - Backpressure stress: artificially delay chunks to force runtime batching changes and verify decoder timing constraints
Scenario F - KV cache variance: run prompts with cold cache and pre-warmed cache and assert output contract stability
Scenario G - Quantized variant mismatch: run fp16 and int8 variants and check for deterministic field types (numbers vs strings) and length-preserving arrays
Chaos tests - randomized token corruption, partial UTF-8 sequences, and injected sentinel tokens to validate graceful degradation paths
notes: Edge-case discovered in spike: some int8 kernels clip trailing commas which turned valid arrays into syntax errors; added test vector to reproduce
test_results: 2026-03-08: initial harness smoke - 120 sessions run, 7 failures (all truncated-object cases). Debug artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-ci/ENG-934512/2026-03-08/
2026-03-11: added tolerant fallback parser - rerun 1k sessions, failures reduced to 2 (both quantized-variant dependent)
